newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs languish in uninspired session.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs languish in uninspired session.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures traded listlessly on Monday as a lack of fresh factors and the impending Lunar New Year and Eid Al-Fitr holidays kept most players from taking new positions.
"It was a typical Monday. Most dealers were looking for direction and local players are all staying flat towards the holidays," said a dealer with an Asian futures house.
Most financial markets in Singapore will be closed on February 7 and 10, and although SIMEX will remain open, dealers said activity was likely to be subdued.
"(March) JGBs are holding well above 126.00. Technically, they look very bullish," said the trader, adding that they faced resistance around 126.60 initially.
They settled at 126.35 against their opening 126.55.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.34 at 1145 GMT against its IMM close at 99.33. December was at 99.21 against 99.20.
Dealers said the Nikkei's slight drop on Monday had no impact on the Japanese interest rate market.

The dollar's relatively unexciting session in forex markets also provided no cues as players turned cautious of pushing the unit higher ahead of a meeting of finance ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) nations this week.
But most dealers remained bullish about the U.S. unit's prospects, seeing any declines on the back of possible G7 pressure as merely providing an opportunity to buy it.
U.S. interest rate futures edged up ahead of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy-setting meeting from Tuesday.
September Eurodollars ended at 94.13 against their IMM close at 94.12.
"The undertone for Eurodollars is influenced by bonds, which are reversing from their recent downturn," said the dealer.
He said the Fed was not expected to raise rates at its meeting this week, but noted that most players were resigned to a rate hike at some point.
"A quarter percent hike is being priced in but anything more would be interesting," he said.
